title: Cloud Detective
desc: A grades 3-5 science investigation about clouds: identify each cloud, what it is like, and the weather it signals.
themeNote: Clouds are examined by observable features (shape, height, color) as evidence for predicting weather.

ui.welcome.title: Cloud Detective
ui.welcome.subtitle: Can you read the story in the sky?
ui.welcome.body: Clouds are clues to tomorrow's weather. Step outside and look up with the cloud detective to investigate nine kinds of clouds: name each one, describe what it is like, and predict the weather it signals.
ui.directions.title: How to investigate each cloud
ui.directions.body1: Study the image and clues. First, identify the cloud. Next, describe what it is like. Finally, choose the weather it signals.
ui.directions.body2: You may revisit exhibits before submitting your final answers.
ui.directions.step1body: Use the clues to name the cloud.
ui.directions.step2body: Choose what the cloud is like.

ui.ace.title: Think it through with ACE
ui.ace.intro: ACE moves you from spotting individual clues to explaining and testing a conclusion — Articulate, Connect, and Extend.
ui.ace.a.title: A — Articulate It
ui.ace.a.q: What do the clues tell you? Explain them in your own words.

ui.ace.e.title: E — Extend It
ui.ace.e.q: Test your conclusion. What else should be true if your answer is correct?

ui.ace.why.body: Students name what they notice, explain how the clues support a conclusion, and test whether that conclusion holds up.

ace.title: The Mystery Sky Line
ace.answer: A contrail — a condensation trail of ice crystals left behind a jet
clues: A long, straight, white line high in the sky
It forms right behind a passing airplane
Made of tiny ice crystals, not smoke
It slowly widens and fades or spreads out
Only appears where jets fly, not lower down
ace.articulate: The clues describe a straight white line made of ice crystals that forms behind a high-flying jet and then spreads or fades.
ace.connect: It reminds me of your breath fogging on a cold day. Warm, moist jet exhaust freezes into ice crystals in the cold air high above, making a cloud in a line.
ace.extend: If it comes from aircraft, it should appear only along flight paths, form best in cold, humid air, and last longer or spread wider when the upper air is moist — behaving like a human-made cloud.
